problem: The constraint Στi = 0 is stated without qualification. It is the usual constraint only when the group sizes are equal; with unequal ni the standard fixed-effects constraint is Σ ni τi = 0, and the (unweighted) Στi = 0 does not make the group effects add to the overall mean.
fix: Write: τi is the fixed effect of group i, with Σ ni τi = 0 (for equal group sizes this reduces to Σ τi = 0), so the effects average out against μ.

where: Section 2, end of the step list
problem: The four model assumptions (independence, normal errors with equal variance, additive effects, robustness) are printed as a plain continuation of the numbered procedure steps. A student revising quickly can read them as further steps to carry out.
fix: Put a heading such as 'Assumptions of the one-way test' before those four bullets so they are clearly separated from the procedure.

problem: 'Ten tests make at least one false alarm likely' overstates the size of the effect. With ten independent 5% tests the chance of at least one false alarm is 1 − 0.95¹⁰ ≈ 0.40, which is substantial but below one half.
fix: Say: 'Ten tests push the chance of at least one false alarm to about 1 − 0.95¹⁰ ≈ 0.40, so a false alarm becomes common even when all machines are equal.'
